module: Neonatal Respiratory Distress and Congenital Thoracic Pathology
subject: ss-paediatric-radiology
title: Pediatric Upper Airway Emergencies: Croup, Epiglottitis and Stridor

steps.say: Croup is the most common cause of acute pediatric stridor. High kilovoltage AP airway radiographs reveal symmetric narrowing of the subglottic trachea, known as the steeple sign.
steps.tx: Recognize the **steeple sign of croup** on an AP neck radiograph. Viral croup (laryngotracheobronchitis), usually caused by parainfluenza virus in infants aged 6 months to 3 years, produces inflammatory mucosal edema in the subglottic trachea. On an AP airway film, loss of the normal square lateral tracheal shoulders produces symmetric, tapered, inverted-V subglottic narrowing resembling a church steeple (Thumbprint sign of epiglottitis).

left.title: Croup (subglottic edema)
points: Symmetric inverted-V steeple sign on AP

steps.say: Acute epiglottitis is a life-threatening airway emergency. A lateral neck radiograph reveals the thumbprint sign from marked swelling of the epiglottis, alongside aryepiglottic fold thickening.
steps.tx: Identify the **thumbprint sign of epiglottitis** on a dedicated lateral neck radiograph. Acute supraglottitis produces profound, life-threatening inflammation of the epiglottis and aryepiglottic folds. On a properly positioned lateral radiograph taken with the neck extended, the swollen, rounded epiglottis resembles the distal phalanx of an adult thumb, obliterating the normal thin valecular air space (Retropharyngeal space normal thickness).

steps.say: Infection in the retropharyngeal space can rapidly compress the airway. Measure the prevertebral soft tissue thickness against cervical vertebral bodies to detect pathological swelling.
steps.tx: Verify the **retropharyngeal space normal thickness** on a true lateral radiograph during full inspiration. The prevertebral soft tissues should measure less than 7 mm (or < 50% C2 body width) anterior to C2, and less than 14 mm in children (equivalent to 100% or the full vertebral body width of C6). Widening beyond these dimensions or gas bubbles indicate retropharyngeal abscess, while expiratory pseudothickening resolves on inspiration (Bacterial tracheitis membrane sign).

rows: < 14 mm in children (100% C6 body width)
True retropharyngeal abscess / danger space extension
Repeat radiograph in full inspiration to confirm

steps.say: Bacterial tracheitis is a dangerous mimicker of croup that fails to respond to racemic epinephrine. Radiographs demonstrate ragged, irregular tracheal mucosal margins.
steps.tx: Recognize the **bacterial tracheitis membrane sign** when a child with apparent croup deteriorates. Bacterial tracheitis (pseudomembranous croup), commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus, produces purulent exudates and mucosal sloughing in the subglottic trachea. Radiographs show irregular, ragged tracheal mucosal contours with floating intraluminal pseudomembranous filling defects that fail to clear with suctioning (Double aortic arch vascular ring).

right.title: Viral croup
points: Rapid response to steroids and nebulizers

steps.say: A double aortic arch is the most common symptomatic complete vascular ring. Contrast esophagography provides clear demonstration of bilateral and posterior esophageal indentations.
steps.tx: Identify a **double aortic arch vascular ring** on barium esophagography and CT angiography. Double aortic arch is the most common symptomatic complete vascular ring, encircling both the trachea and esophagus. Frontal esophagram shows bilateral compressive indentations on the esophagus (the right arch is usually larger and higher), while the lateral view shows a deep posterior esophageal indentation, causing persistent biphasic stridor and dysphagia (Pulmonary artery sling anatomy).

rows: Right and left aortic arches compressing lumen
Determines dominant arch (usually right) for surgery

steps.say: A pulmonary artery sling is the only vascular anomaly that courses between the trachea and the esophagus. An anterior indentation on the esophagus is the hallmark finding.
steps.tx: Diagnose **pulmonary artery sling anatomy** on barium esophagography and cross-sectional imaging. In a pulmonary artery sling, the anomalous left pulmonary artery arises from the right pulmonary artery, arching over the right main bronchus and coursing between the posterior trachea and anterior esophagus. It produces a pathognomonic anterior indentation on the esophagus, frequently accompanied by complete cartilaginous tracheal rings (Inhaled radiolucent foreign body).

steps.say: Organic foreign body aspiration produces dynamic air trapping. A ball-valve bronchial obstruction traps air during expiration, shifting the mediastinum away from the affected side.
steps.tx: Detect an **inhaled radiolucent foreign body** using dynamic expiratory or bilateral decubitus radiographs. Organic foreign body aspiration (peanuts, food) causes a partial ball-valve bronchial obstruction that allows air entry during inspiration but blocks egress during expiration. This mechanism leads to dynamic air trapping with hyperlucency, hyperinflation of the affected lung, and mediastinal shift away from the affected side on expiration (Laryngomalacia dynamic collapse).

nodes.label: Shift of mediastinum to contralateral side

steps.say: Laryngomalacia is the leading cause of congenital stridor in newborns, accounting for sixty to seventy percent of cases. Dynamic fluoroscopy demonstrates inspiratory collapse of supraglottic structures.
steps.tx: Demonstrate **laryngomalacia dynamic collapse** on dynamic airway fluoroscopy or cine MRI. Laryngomalacia is the leading cause of congenital stridor (60-70%), diagnosed definitively by flexible laryngoscopy showing an omega-shaped epiglottis and inspiratory inward collapse of arytenoids into the laryngeal vestibule. Dynamic fluoroscopy confirms collapse of the supraglottic airway during inspiration that resolves during expiration and improves when the infant is prone.

rows: Dynamic inspiratory collapse; normal at rest
Fixed circumferential narrowing across all phases
